_method: Hand key for usage_coverage_sample.json -- a uniform random sample (seed 20260727, n=60) drawn from the COMPLETE population of usage-register-overlap fires on claims the current three signals (apposition, definition-marker, gloss-overlap) do NOT make. Judged reading only word+text+work, against PRECISION-STANDARD.md's standard: does the passage supply an explicit or strongly implicit cue (synonym, restatement, apposition, stated contrast, categorical list, functional definition) for the word's meaning-as-used-here, or does it merely fail to contradict a meaning the reader already carries in.
_calibration_note: First pass: 29/60 = 48.3% informative. Rereading against the standard's own worked examples -- specifically the 'hammer'/'a head like a hammer' case, where a simile assumes the reader already knows the vehicle concept and explains nothing -- caught three initial True calls (drunken/'reeled like a drunken giant', curtain/'a curtain of tangled sprays and branches', delightful/paired only with the equally-unexplained 'delicious') using the candidate word as the FAMILIAR reference term in a simile or loose adjective pairing, not as the word being taught. Reversed to False on rereading. Final: 27/60 = 45.0% informative, 95% Wilson CI [33.1%, 57.5%]. Recorded here because the same first-pass-too-generous pattern PRECISION-STANDARD.md documented on its own frozen sample (61.7% -> 50.0%) reproduced itself on this one, and the correction is the finding, not a footnote.
